attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: Keeps the hedges ('perhaps', 'probably') and the firm upper bound. Only 'certainly not hundreds of billions' is unhedged. The two lower bands are hedged and so not scored.

contract.note: Reading 'made' as cumulative realized revenue through the post date is an ordinary reading, and the contract flags the revenue-versus-profit ambiguity. It correctly marks only the hundreds-of-billions bound as firm and excludes forecasts and run rates.

evidence.note: A pre-post S&P forecast of about $3.7B full-year 2023 genAI software revenue. It is a full-year forecast, not cumulative realized revenue through Aug 14, so under the contract it can neither support nor contradict.

reviews.rationale: Only the firm part ('certainly not hundreds of billions') can be scored. The hundreds-of-millions and not-billions bands are hedged, so they are not adjudicable. The packet's only item is a full-year 2023 forecast, which the contract excludes as proof of cumulative realized revenue. That forecast makes $100B+ look implausible, but no realized cumulative estimate through Aug 14, 2023 is in the packet, so the firm bound is not settled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the approximate $100B scale, 'so far', and 'vastly exceeds'. The revenue scope in context, including driver assistance, appears in the contract rather than the proposition, which is acceptable.

contract.note: The contract includes the driver-assistance revenue Marcus himself named. It treats $100B as an order of magnitude and 'vastly' as a large multiple without imposing a ratio. It requires a matched cumulative comparison, which is reasonable.

evidence.note: Ford's estimate (Oct 2022), reproduced by a secondary site, of more than $100B invested in Level 4 autonomy. It backs the investment scale but gives no revenue side, so the comparison is not established.
Mobileye's Q4 2022 revenue of $565M is one firm's quarterly figure in the named driver-assistance segment. It cannot establish cumulative industry revenue.

reviews.rationale: The investment scale is roughly corroborated by Ford's more-than-$100B estimate for Level 4. However, the packet has no cumulative industry revenue figure covering the driver-assistance and robotaxi businesses Marcus included, only one Mobileye quarter. The comparison at the heart of 'vastly exceeds' therefore cannot be checked against the packet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own view, stated in the first person in his post.

semantics.note: This revision restores the 'I don't think' framing, so the claim reads as a hedged personal view. It gives a vague, qualitative risk judgment with no threshold or timeframe. The 2024 date belongs to the rumor he discusses, not to his claim.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to invent a timeframe or distress thresholds. 'Imminent danger' and 'out of the woods' have no measurable meaning, and treating later survival as proof would replace his claim with a different one.

evidence.note: OpenAI's Jan 2023 announcement of a multibillion-dollar Microsoft investment. It is a company disclosure and gives financial-backing context only.

reviews.rationale: This is a hedged opinion ('I don't think') built on vague terms ('imminent danger', 'out of the woods') with no measure or timeframe. The policy treats graded belief as not scored, and no fair support or contradiction condition can be set. The case itself is intact; the claim simply cannot be scored.
